---
title: Files
description: How Marfa keeps a file's bytes once, however many items name them, who may read them, and how long they stay.
job: A builder learns how a file's bytes are kept once, who may read them and how long they stay.
kind: concept
---

**A file in Marfa is two things.** The bytes are a **blob**, stored once under a hash of their content. The file is an **item** naming the blob by that hash and holding everything else: a title, a media type, an image's size. An item stays small enough for every working copy to hold.

## A blob and the item that names it

To add a file, upload its bytes, then create an item naming the hash Marfa answers:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa blobs upload inventory.txt
```

```text
stored sha256:7fc0ba0d4e6818ccf1f3eae53ed1ce059625672ff5438d0ab59b12ab6e0305ef (64 bytes, text/plain)
```

</Terminal>

A file item has the type `core.file` or one beneath it, such as `core.file.image`. Its `blob_ref` is the hash, `sha256:` and 64 hex digits:

```http title="Request"
POST /items
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "type": "core.file",
  "properties": {
    "title": "Flat inventory",
    "blob_ref": "sha256:7fc0ba0d4e6818ccf1f3eae53ed1ce059625672ff5438d0ab59b12ab6e0305ef",
    "mime_type": "text/plain"
  }
}
```

Marfa sets `size_bytes` itself. [Upload and download files](/build/files-upload-download) walks through the rest.

**Adding the same bytes again stores nothing more, and Marfa doesn't say so:** check first, as `marfa items add` does. [Find items by blob](/reference/api/items/findItemsByBlob), or `marfa items blobs`, answers up to 20 items for each of up to 200 SHA-256 hashes. It leaves out items in the bin, `system.*` and `app.*` items and what the credential can't list, and answers no items for a hash none of the rest holds, even one Marfa keeps.

## Find a file by what it says

**Marfa reads the text inside files,** such as a PDF's pages or a photo's text by OCR, onto the item as `extracted_text`, which search matches. An image also gains its `width` and `height`, and a recording its `duration`, for the kinds and sizes Marfa supports. The owner can turn text reading, or OCR alone, off in [Settings](/run/settings).

## Who may read a blob

**Knowing a hash isn't enough.** A credential reads a blob through an item it can read that names it: a file item, or an item with the hash in its text, such as an image in a note's body. A reference lends its read only if its writer had uploaded the bytes or could already read them, so a hash found somewhere grants nothing. A write giving a file item a new `blob_ref` its writer can't prove is refused `404 blob_not_found`.

Reading a blob no readable item names is `404 blob_not_found`, as for one that doesn't exist, **even one you just uploaded.** Create the item straight after uploading: by default, an unnamed blob is purged a day or more after upload. A credential holding `blobs.manage` reads every blob.

A page or player that can't send a credential uses a **signed link** from `marfa blobs url`, good for an hour by default and seven days at most.

## How long a blob stays

A blob stays while something names it, even an item in the bin or an earlier version of one. Once nothing does, a later [housekeeping](/run/check-health) run purges it, by default at least a day after it was found unnamed, never while a backup Marfa keeps still names it. Blobs sit on the disk beside the server, and [Back up and restore](/run/back-up-and-restore#use-an-object-store) can add copies elsewhere.

The rules behind this page are in the [blobs](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/blobs.md), [stores](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/stores.md), and [items](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/items.md#itemsblobs) chapters of the contract.
